description: agent-symbiont fleet: self-evolving binaries reporting evolution pipeline health, LLM token consumption, revision registry state and the trading performance of the code the LLM just wrote. Designed for many concurrent instances -- filter via the model/instance variables; all timeseries break down per instance. Events arrive in bursts (a refinement round every ~2-3 min), so all rates/ratios/means use fixed 30m windows -- short windows render as unreadable combs and zero-valued stats. The Training harness / Pareto frontier / Last evaluated candidate / Persistence rows cover the agent_symbiont_* series emitted by the agent-symbiont harness on top of the framework. NOTE: neither exporter configures histogram bucket bounds, so every histogram is exported as a summary whose quantile series only hold the exporter's 60s rolling window and read 0 in between, while _sum/_count stay cumulative -- hence means are derived from rate(_sum)/rate(_count) and the quantile panels filter != 0 and span the gaps.
title: symbiont

panels.description: Number of symbiont instances currently reporting metrics (matching the model/instance filters).
panels.title: Instances

panels.description: Completed agentic LLM runs per hour across the selected fleet, smoothed over a 30-minute window.
panels.title: LLM runs / h

panels.description: Fraction of evolution attempts that produced an activated revision (activations / attempts). The complement is the failure ratio (parse / compile / signature / no_rust_code).
panels.title: Attempt success ratio

panels.description: Failed evolution attempts per hour across the fleet (all failure kinds).
panels.title: Evolve failures / h

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration of Runtime::evolve calls (including retries), derived from the summary _sum/_count.
panels.title: Mean evolve duration

panels.description: LLM output tokens produced by the selected fleet over the last 24h (increase over a fixed 24h window, robust to process restarts / counter resets).
panels.title: Output tokens (24h)

panels.description: Failed evolution attempts per hour by failure kind (parse / compile / signature / no_rust_code), summed across selected instances. Compile failures dominating suggests prompt or crate-context issues.
panels.title: Evolve failures / h by kind

panels.description: Revision activations per hour per instance -- the fleet's effective evolution throughput.
panels.title: Revision activations / h by instance

panels.description: Mean attempts per Runtime::evolve call per instance (1 = first-try success). Rising values mean the model needs more retries to produce loadable code.
panels.title: Mean attempts per evolve by instance

panels.description: Mean duration per evolution pipeline stage (llm / parse_validate / compile / load), derived from summary _sum/_count. Log scale: llm dominates by orders of magnitude.
panels.title: Mean stage duration

panels.description: Mean wall-clock Runtime::evolve duration (including retries) per instance. Slow instances point at contended LLM backends or slow compile hosts.
panels.title: Mean evolve duration by instance

panels.description: Token consumption per second by kind (input / cached_input / output), summed across selected instances, smoothed over 30m. cached_input is cheap; watch fresh input + output for cost.
panels.title: Token rate by kind

panels.description: Total token consumption per second per instance (all kinds). Identifies which fleet members burn the most LLM capacity.
panels.title: Token rate by instance

panels.description: Mean tokens and messages per agentic run (fleet-wide, from summary _sum/_count). Growing input tokens per run = context bloat in the evolution prompts.
panels.title: Mean tokens & messages per run

panels.description: Completed agentic runs per hour by outcome, plus transient LLM retries per hour. Anything other than `ok` deserves a look at the logs; rising retries point at a flaky LLM backend.
panels.title: LLM runs / h by outcome

panels.description: Revisions retained in the keep-all registry per instance. Grows monotonically; watch alongside dylib size for disk usage (~49 MB per dylib observed).
panels.title: Revisions loaded & active id by instance

panels.description: Mean generated Rust source size and compiled dylib size per revision (fleet-wide, from summary _sum/_count). Log scale: dylibs are ~4 orders of magnitude larger than their source.
panels.title: Mean artifact size per revision

panels.description: Backtest throughput across selected instances, summed over splits (train/test) and phases (fresh rounds / frontier re-evaluation).
panels.title: Backtests / s

panels.description: Fraction of backtests aborted early because the evolved code panicked. A rising ratio means the LLM generates crashier code.
panels.title: Backtest panic ratio

panels.description: Completed refinement rounds per hour (evolve + evaluate + persist), all outcomes.
panels.title: Rounds / h

panels.description: Fraction of refinement rounds that completed (outcome ok); the complement aborted the training run on a failed evolution.
panels.title: Round success ratio

panels.description: Time since the most recent successfully completed training run. Training runs daily; alert past ~26h.
panels.title: Since last successful train

panels.description: Backtest throughput broken down by dataset split (train/test) and phase (fresh candidate rounds vs. frontier re-evaluation). rate() of a counter, robust across process restarts.
panels.title: Backtests / s by split & phase

panels.description: Backtests aborted early by a panic in the evolved code, per hour. Should be near zero; spikes correlate with prompt or prelude changes.
panels.title: Backtest panics / h by split & phase

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration of one evaluation pass (all datasets x all matrix configurations), derived from _sum/_count rates.

targets.expr: sum by (split, phase) (rate(agent_symbiont_evaluation_duration_seconds_sum{model=~"$model",instance=~"$instance"}[30m])) / sum by (split, phase) (rate(agent_symbiont_evaluation_duration_seconds_count{model=~"$model",instance=~"$instance"}[30m]))

panels.title: Mean evaluation duration by split & phase

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration of one full refinement round (evolve + train/test evaluation + persistence). The evolve share alone is symbiont_evolve_duration_seconds.
panels.title: Mean round duration by instance

panels.description: Refinement rounds per hour by outcome (ok / evolve_failed / error), 30m smoothed.
panels.title: Rounds / h by outcome

panels.description: Frontier verdicts per hour by phase and verdict. phase=round covers freshly evolved candidates -- its entered share is the key signal that the agentic loop still produces improving candidates. phase=frontier_reeval covers retained incumbents re-scored on the slid dataset window: entered means the incumbent survived the slide, dominated/rejected_* means it was pruned.
panels.title: Frontier verdicts / h by phase & verdict

panels.description: Quality-gate criteria violated by evaluated candidates, per hour by criterion (30m smoothed, phase=round). Only liquidation and invalid_metrics (SAFETY) reject a candidate; the rest are advisory feedback. The dominating criterion is the gate to tune or the defect the agent must engineer away.
panels.title: Quality gate failures / h by criterion

panels.description: Backtests aggregated into the most recent train-split sweep of a fresh candidate: days x evaluation-matrix configurations (44 x 135 = 5940 for the default window). The denominator of the panic count next to it, and the sanity check that the distribution panels below summarize a complete sweep -- the histogram's own _count is cumulative across candidates and cannot serve as one.
panels.title: Backtests in last sweep

panels.description: Backtests of the most recent sweep that aborted early because the evolved code panicked. Unlike agent_symbiont_backtest_panics_total this is not cumulative: it describes only the code evaluated last, so any non-zero value means the candidate being worked on right now is crashy.
panels.title: Panicking backtests (last sweep)

panels.description: Time since the last-evaluation series were written. One refinement round (evolve + evaluate + persist) takes ~2-3 min, so a value far above that means training is stalled or the harness is between runs.
panels.title: Since last evaluation

panels.description: Mean per-backtest return on equity of the code evaluated last, train split, all phases. Derived from rate(_sum)/rate(_count) of the histogram: both are cumulative, so unlike the quantile series this never drains between evaluations. One backtest = one day under one matrix configuration.
panels.title: Mean return / backtest (train)

panels.description: The same figure on the held-out test window the agent never sees. Persistently below the train figure = the generated code is overfitting the training window.
panels.title: Mean return / backtest (test)

panels.description: Mean per-backtest surefire ratio (integrated upside/downside x return in excess of buy-and-hold) on the train split -- the per-backtest cousin of the pareto reward. The frontier's actual reward is a family-weighted median taken at admission time and lives in ClickHouse (agent_rounds.train_reward), not in Prometheus.
panels.title: Mean surefire ratio (train)

panels.description: Mean per-backtest return on equity, by dataset split and phase. train/round is the freshly evolved candidate, test/round the held-out window, */frontier_reeval a retained incumbent re-scored on the slid dataset window. Means come from rate(_sum)/rate(_count) and are therefore continuous; the panel to the right shows the spread within one candidate.

targets.expr: sum by (split, phase) (rate(agent_symbiont_last_eval_metric_sum{metric="return_on_equity_pct",model=~"$model",instance=~"$instance"}[30m])) / sum by (split, phase) (rate(agent_symbiont_last_eval_metric_count{metric="return_on_equity_pct",model=~"$model",instance=~"$instance"}[30m]))

panels.title: Mean return on equity per backtest by split & phase

panels.description: Robustness spread of the code evaluated last across the 135 evaluation-matrix configurations (starting position x latency x balance x fee level): worst cell, median, best cell. These are summary quantiles over the harness exporter's 60s rolling window, so they read 0 between evaluations -- the query drops the zeros and the line spans the gaps, giving one point cluster per evaluated candidate. A deep worst cell under a healthy median means the strategy only works in favourable cells.
panels.title: Return on equity spread across the matrix (train, fresh candidates)

panels.description: Mean per-backtest surefire ratio (integrated upside/downside x excess return vs buy-and-hold) by split and phase. This is the objective the agentic loop optimizes, so the train/test gap here is the generalization gap of the code being written right now.

targets.expr: sum by (split, phase) (rate(agent_symbiont_last_eval_metric_sum{metric="surefire_ratio",model=~"$model",instance=~"$instance"}[30m])) / sum by (split, phase) (rate(agent_symbiont_last_eval_metric_count{metric="surefire_ratio",model=~"$model",instance=~"$instance"}[30m]))

panels.title: Mean surefire ratio per backtest by split & phase

panels.description: Per-backtest equity drawdown of the code evaluated last: the continuous mean from rate(_sum)/rate(_count), plus the p95 tail read from the exporter's 60s rolling window (zeros dropped, hence gappy). The p95 drawdown over the train sweep is the pareto risk objective the frontier minimizes.
panels.title: Drawdown per backtest: mean & p95 (fresh candidates)

panels.description: Observed values of the family-weighted quality-gate criteria for the last evaluated candidate -- the same numbers rendered into the agent's prompt. Gauges, so continuous. Requirements: active_rate >= 75%, p25_turnover >= 0.1%, p25_excess_return >= -0.5%, p95_failure_rate <= 10%, p95_dropped_command_rate <= 1%, p95_forced_cancel_rate <= 1%, liquidation = 0, invalid_metrics = 0. The last two are SAFETY criteria and reject a candidate outright; the rest are advisory optimization targets. How often each one is violated is the 'Quality gate failures / h' panel above.
panels.title: Quality gate observations: rates (train, fresh candidates)

panels.description: The two count-scaled quality-gate criteria of the last evaluated candidate: p25 genuine fills per backtest (require >= 1, i.e. the strategy must actually trade) and p95 submitted orders per day (require <= 14400 = 10/min). Log scale, since the two differ by orders of magnitude.
panels.title: Quality gate observations: counts (train, fresh candidates)

panels.description: Mean ClickHouse insert latency by store (backtest results, generated candidates, evolve failures), derived from _sum/_count rates.
panels.title: Mean insert duration by store

panels.description: Failed ClickHouse inserts per hour by store. Any non-zero rate stalls or aborts training runs.
panels.title: Insert failures / h by store
